title: an inferred-fallible callback reaching a consumer through an ARRAY spread of a named local must spell a Result contract
notes: specification/failures.mdx, 'Inference and Public Contracts': 'Public, abstract, ambient, and declaration-only contracts MUST express fallibility directly with `Result<A, E>` or `Promise<Result<A, E>>`.' A callback boundary is a VALUE edge, not an argument position: the callee invokes a function it received inside an object literal, an array literal, a parenthesis, a cast or a `new` argument list exactly as it invokes one passed directly. Fail-closed matters here because the accepting behaviour is silent and wrong rather than loud and wrong — R1FIX executed this class before the fix and measured `isOk() === true` with a `Result` sitting in the SUCCESS payload, with zero language diagnostics and zero emitted-TypeScript diagnostics. An array spread's elements ARE syntactically present, so the walk can name them and does; the diagnostic lands on `one`, the local the spread carries. An OBJECT spread is deliberately different — its members are not syntactically present at the spread site — and both backends still accept a fallible callback reaching a consumer through `{ ...base }`. That gap is fail-open on BOTH backends, is recorded as STOP-2 in the R1FIX and CONV reports with a reproduction at `<scratchpad>/conv/probes/hb13-object-spread-argument/main.sm`, and no case here pins it in either direction, because closing it needs the value-escape analysis both lanes stopped on rather than a wider syntactic walk.
